newsitem.title: CHINA: China July forex reserves $90.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: China July forex reserves $90.8 billion.

text.p: China's foreign exchange reserves reached a record $90.8 billion in July and could reach nearly $100 billion by the end of 1996, the Business News on Saturday quoted the governor of the central bank as saying.
It quoted Dai Xianglong as telling a meeting in Beijing on Friday that the supply of foreign exchange would exceed demand in the near future.
He said annual price inflation for the full 1996 year could be controlled at between seven and eight percent.
The government target is 10 percent. Annual retail price inflation in all 1995 was 14.8 percent over the year before.
Dai said that China's gross domestic product would continue to grow at a fast rate this year. The original target was growth of eight percent but it could be higher than nine percent, he said.
Commenting on a cut in interest rates which took effect on Friday, Dai said that the cut was possible because of a sharp fall in prices and would benefit the management of state companies.
"Over the next several years, we will still adopt an appropriately tight monetary policy," he said.
The central bank cut bank deposit and lending rates by an average 1.5 and 1.2 percentage points respectively.
Annual inflation fell to 5.8 percent in July, well below the annual target of 10 percent.
